newsitem.title: USA: U.S. producer prices tumble in April.
newsitem.headline: U.S. producer prices tumble in April.

text.p: Producer prices posted their biggest decline in nearly four years in April, tumbling by 0.6 percent as food and energy costs declined, the Labor Department said on Wednesday.

This was the fourth straight month that producer prices have fallen and followed a 0.1 percent decline in March. Excluding volatile food and energy costs, producer prices fell by 0.1 percent in April, after a 0.4 percent rise in March.

The steep drop in producer prices in April should temper concerns on Wall Street that the inflation-wary Federal Reserve will raise interest rates at a meeting next Tuesday, but the decline was unlikely to extinguish those fears completely.
Wall Street analysts had expected producer prices to hold steady in May. Excluding volatile food and energy costs, producer prices had been expected to post a 0.1 percent gain.
The April drop in producer prices was widespread.
Energy prices continued their recent decline, falling by an additional 2.6 percent in April, led by weaker gasoline prices.

After surging in March, food prices also dropped in April. Vegetable prices plunged by more than 20 percent, while fruit prices fell nearly 5 percent. The recent steep rise in coffee prices slowed, with prices increasing by nearly 5 percent in April after a gain of almost 13 percent in March.
Prices for a variety of items outside the volatile food and energy sectors also declined in April.
Car prices dropped by 0.5 percent, computer prices by 4.1 percent and civilian aircraft prices by 2 percent.
Tobacco prices, which rose a whopping 2.5 percent in March, increased 0.9 percent in April.
The producer price report also showed that there is little in the way of inflation in the pipeline.

Intermediate goods, which are used to make the finished products that comprise the producer price index, fell by 0.3 percent in April. Prices of crude goods, materials at the start of the production process, dropped by 0.9 percent last month.
